payload.root_cause: In src/text.js, slugify's whitespace-collapsing replace uses the regex /[\s-]+/ WITHOUT the global flag (src/text.js:11). String.prototype.replace with a non-global regex performs only ONE substitution, so only the first run of whitespace/dashes is converted to a dash; all subsequent gaps are left as raw spaces. For 'Hello Big World!': toLowerCase -> 'hello big world!'; strip invalid chars (line 10, which does have /g) -> 'hello big world'; single replace -> 'hello-big world'; leading/trailing dash trim (line 12) -> 'hello-big world' — exactly the reported output. The fix is to add the g flag: .replace(/[\s-]+/g, '-').

payload.rationale: The whitespace-collapsing step in slugify (src/text.js:11) uses the regex /[\s-]+/ without the global flag. String.prototype.replace performs only a single substitution for non-global regexes, so only the first run of whitespace/dashes becomes a dash and later gaps remain as raw spaces (e.g. 'Hello Big World!' -> 'hello-big world'). Adding the g flag makes replace substitute every run, matching the behavior of the surrounding regexes on lines 10 and 12 (both already global) and the expected outputs in test/text.test.js ('hello-big-world', 'already-slugged-title'). This is a one-character fix to the root cause.
